<reason>Side A (CON) anchored the debate to the resolution as written — crewed exploration justified *by unmapped seafloor* — and then showed the remedy does not serve that warrant. Its strongest strategic move was refusing the austerity frame ("give the ocean a space-scale budget; I'll spend every dollar"), which stripped PRO of the ambition-versus-stinginess contrast and forced the clash onto the single word "crewed." PRO's reframe ("the warrant is an unread planet"; human presence creates political authorization and public infrastructure) was genuinely interesting and well phrased, but its load-bearing causal claim was tested and never repaired: CON's Shuttle/station-versus-probes point and the sixty-years-of-crewed-submergence-without-an-ocean-Apollo point put real pressure on the "crews unlock new money" mechanism, and PRO's reply ("that's just how one agency splits a pot it already has; the ocean never got the pot") is unfalsifiable and was neatly turned by CON's "that is exactly the pot the ocean would get." CON's pressure question Q2 was the pivot of the debate: PRO answered honestly ("yes, put people in even if robots raster faster"), which was creditable candor but conceded that the motion's stated warrant is not what its remedy serves — and CON crystallized precisely that in closing. Both sides handled A1:/A2: labelling correctly; both had one clipped turn, so that cost cancels. CON's specificity (approximate share of seafloor charted at modern resolution) was cautiously worded ordinary background knowledge rather than brittle fake precision, and it directly answered the mechanism question. PRO argued well and memorably, but left the decisive burden — why crewed presence, rather than scaled autonomy, follows from unmapped seafloor — standing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Q2 ("if an all-uncrewed program would finish the map decades sooner, do you still put people in the sphere?") plus PRO's honest "Yes" and CON's exploitation of it: the motion's warrant is coverage, and PRO admitted the crew is not what fills the blank. Combined with CON's Shuttle-versus-probes turn on the political-will mechanism, this closed PRO's main route.</best_rebuttal>
